worldcombat.skill.kowtowcleave.summary: Kowtow first to bait the foe into closing in or striking at you, then lunge in and land the cut on that moment's opening; it only connects at true contact with a clear line, makes no accuracy roll once in contact, and knocks the target back on a hit. If the bait does not take, it still swings the one cut; if it cannot catch up, is walled off, or the target leaves, it swings at nothing, and an empty aim swings too.
worldcombat.skill.kowtowcleave.descripti: The slash deals about %1$s damage with no accuracy roll once in contact; if the target took the bait during the kowtow, its power is %2$s higher.

The kowtow only baits the original target within %1$s blocks: it counts if that target really closed at least 0.4 blocks toward you, or really made one native attack against you during the bow. Even without the bait, the cut still goes out.

After the bow the user closes each tick along the aim by %1$s blocks, with the move's range as the total budget; the first non-friendly body truly reached takes the blade, a hit knocks it back %2$s blocks with a %3$s block hit radius. When the budget runs out, a wall blocks the way, or it cannot move, it swings at nothing on the spot.
The bow and the blade are %1$s s apart.
worldcombat.skill.kowtowcleave.timing: Range %1$s blocks, windup %2$s s, recover %3$s s, costs %4$s PP, cooldown %5$s s.
worldcombat.skill.kowtowcleave.growth.1: At level %1$s: slash power %2$s, lunge step %3$s blocks.
worldcombat.skill.kowtowcleave.use.1: Land a heavier cut on a target that took the bait
worldcombat.skill.kowtowcleave.use.2: Close along the aim; the first body reached takes the blade
worldcombat.skill.kowtowcleave.preferenc: On: a deeper kowtow gives +0.15 opening bonus when the bait works, but 4 ticks more windup and 6 ticks more cooldown. Off: a quick bow and cut, cheaper and faster.
Beyond this distance the user closes in instead of kowtowing. Larger values let it pounce from further.
On: the user may leave its post to close on a target; off: it only strikes from where it stands.
